correctness.rationale: For exact Weibull W and independent Gamma(ceil(W),1) durations, h_n=(log n)^(1/beta) and b_n=h_n^(1-beta)/beta give a Poisson extreme process. The Gamma exponential-Chernoff bound proves an all-jobs lower-workload cutoff for beta<=1/2. At beta<1/2 mark error is negligible; at beta=1/2 the Gaussian mark produces the exact PPP void probability p_star; at beta>1/2 a diverging independent collection of O(sqrt(h_n))-nearby workloads defeats the workload leader. The displayed integral identity follows by integration by parts. Reproducibility script passed 3009 finite consistency checks, but the proof does not rely on finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: Identifies a sharp and nontrivial natural selection transition in stochastic workload/service systems, where heavy-tailed latent workload spacing competes with its associated square-root service noise. The critical shape 1/2 and nontrivial computable limiting winner probability distinguish this result from mere extrema normalization, and address a motivated analogous question to deepest-versus-longest ranking.
